 Employees Provident Fund (EPF) CEO Ahmad Zulqarnain Onn -AZMAN GHANI/The Star 
 PETALING JAYA: The Employees Provident Fund’s (EPF) income growth for the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 decelerated a little – registering just a 3% growth from the same quarter last year. 
 In a statement, the retirement fund said total investment income for the quarter under review stood at RM25.82bil, compared to RM25.07bil last year.
 EPF chief executive officer, Ahmad Zulqarnain Onn said he expects the trend to continue into the next quarter amidst weaknesses in global stock markets and rising yields in the bond markets.
 According to him, at the start of the third quarter, risks around government borrowing, continued inflation and the valuation of AI-related stocks became elevated.
 “These developments require us to be disciplined in managing the portfolio, balancing opportunities against emerging risks while remaining focused on sustainable long-term returns and the retirement security of our members,” he said.
 For the quarter, equities income increased 3% to RM17.41bil supported by healthy global equity markets that enabled EPF’s fund managers to manage the portfolio and generate value.
 Fixed income instruments comprising Malaysian Government Securities and Equivalents, as well as Loans and Bonds, contributed RM7.12bil for the quarter.
 Total investment assets stood at RM1.55 trillion with 38% invested globally.
 Meanwhile, the fund saw a 30% increase in its total investment income for the first nine months of 2026 ended Sept 30, 2026.
 In a statement, the retirement fund said it recorded RM83.32bil for the period versus RM63.99bil for the same period a year ago.
 For the nine months, voluntary contributions rose to RM18.27bil, reflecting continued interest among members in building additional retirement savings beyond mandatory contributions.
